sun.name: Sun
sun.description: The star at the centre of the Solar System. Its gravity holds the planets in orbit and its light and heat support life on Earth.
facts: Holds about 99.8% of the Solar System's mass.
Is about 4.6 billion years old.
Produces energy by nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Its diameter is about 109 times Earth's.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.description: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.
facts: Orbits the Sun once every 88 Earth days.
Has no moons.
Has almost no atmosphere, so temperatures swing from about 430 C by day to about -180 C at night.

venus.name: Venus
venus.description: The second planet from the Sun, similar in size to Earth but covered in thick clouds.
facts: The hottest planet, with surface temperatures around 465 C.
Its atmosphere is mostly carbon dioxide with clouds of sulphuric acid.
Rotates backwards (retrograde) compared with most planets.
A day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days).
Has no moons.

earth.name: Earth
earth.description: The third planet from the Sun and the only one known to support life.
facts: About 71% of its surface is covered by water.
Has one natural satellite, the Moon.
Orbits the Sun at about 150 million km (1 astronomical unit).
One orbit takes about 365.25 days.

mars.name: Mars
mars.description: The fourth planet, a cold desert world known as the Red Planet.
facts: Its red colour comes from iron oxide (rust) in its dust.
Has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.
Home to Olympus Mons, the largest known volcano in the Solar System.
A Martian day is about 24 hours 37 minutes.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.description: The largest planet, a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
facts: More than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.
The Great Red Spot is a giant storm larger than Earth.
Has the shortest day of any planet, about 10 hours.
Its four largest moons, the Galilean moons, are Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.description: The sixth planet, a gas giant famous for its bright ring system.
facts: Its rings are made mostly of ice particles with some rock.
Its average density is lower than water's.
Its largest moon, Titan, has a thick nitrogen atmosphere.
Takes about 29 Earth years to orbit the Sun.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.description: The seventh planet, an ice giant that spins on its side.
facts: Its axis is tilted about 98 degrees, so it rolls around the Sun on its side.
Methane in its atmosphere gives it a blue-green colour.
Was the first planet discovered with a telescope, by William Herschel in 1781.
Takes about 84 Earth years to orbit the Sun.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.description: The eighth and farthest known planet from the Sun, a deep-blue ice giant.
facts: Has the strongest winds measured in the Solar System, over 2,000 km/h.
Was found in 1846 using mathematical predictions rather than by searching the sky at random.
Its largest moon, Triton, orbits backwards (retrograde).
Takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun.
